title: I host an overnight radio show alone. A caller keeps hearing my words before they air.
story:
The caller laughed at my joke while I was still telling it.

I'm the overnight host at a tiny station outside town. Just me, a microphone, and a dark producer's booth behind a glass window, empty since the budget cuts. Everything I say goes out on a seven second delay, in case someone swears on air.

She'd called every night that week. Soft voice. Same request. "Keep talking. I like hearing you."

Tonight, while she was on the line, I could hear her radio in the background. My own voice. But there was no delay. Every word came out of her speaker the instant I said it.

"Where are you listening from?" I asked. "Close," she whispered.

So I tested her. I muted my mic and started a song. Through the phone, no song played. I just heard my own breathing, a little louder than it should be.

The only place you can hear me without the delay is right here, in this room.

I turned my chair slowly toward the booth. The glass was black. Just my reflection, and the empty dark behind it.

The line clicked off.

Behind the glass, a phone lit up.
premise: overnight radio host's regular caller hears him with no broadcast delay; the only place without the delay is the studio, and she is in the dark producer's booth behind the glass
theme: night shift at a radio station
